subject: Renewal uplift & commit velocity — conditional rebate scheduler
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jordan <alex.jordan@healthlyx.com>, Procurement Team <procure@healthlyx.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal uplift & commit velocity — conditional rebate scheduler

Hi Alex / Procurement team,

Following up from our call last week — thanks again for the transparency on usage growth. You mentioned a likely ~30% uplift in token usage over the next 12 months tied to the new feature rollout. To make the renewal straight-forward for your finance team while preserving pricing predictability, we modeled two paths and attached a workbook with numbers:

Option 1 — Accelerated Uplift + Tiered Rebate
- Immediate uplift to 1.3x current commit; 8% rebate applied retroactively once quarterly usage sustains above 115% for two consecutive quarters.
- Invoices pro-rated on the next bill cycle; rebate applied as credit on the following invoice.

Option 2 — Staged Top-up & Co-term
- Staged top-up (50% now, 50% at co-term) with a smaller guaranteed discount (5%) and an operational credit if top-up not consumed within 9 months.
- Falls back to current pricing should usage not materialize.

Questions we need from you to finalize the proposal:
1) Confirm target uplift (is ~30% final?) and the expected PO/approval date window.
2) Preferred billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly invoicing).
3) Any must-have payment terms (net30/45/60) or required invoice fields for your AP team.

I attached a spreadsheet with line-by-line impact and a draft mutual action plan. If procurement would like, we can convert the selected path into a DocuSign-ready amendment.

Next step: if you can respond with notes above by EOD Tuesday (15th), we’ll lock the final amendment and route to legal.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0182

Kimberly — thanks for the options and the quick turnaround. A few clarifying items from procurement and legal so we can align timelines:

- Invoice/proration: when you say "pro-rated on the next bill cycle," can you confirm exact proration math? We need a line-item that shows partial-month adjustments and a projected first three invoices.
- Rebate triggers: for Option 1, what metrics will you use to verify the 115% sustained usage threshold? Is this measured by billed tokens or by API request count?
- Payment terms: we typically do net45; however, if there is an early-payment discount available that could be considered.
- Legal review: we may need to redline the amendment. Our counsel requires a 10 business day review window. Will Redwood accept that window without holding the current pricing?

We are targeting a PO by 1 July if we can get clarity on the proration and rebate definition. I’ve looped in Procurement for the PO logistics.

—Alex
Alex Jordan
Head of Platform Engineering | HealthlyX
alex.jordan@healthlyx.com

Subject: Re: Renewal uplift & commit velocity — conditional rebate scheduler

Hi Alex — Ben here (Sales Director). Quick answers below and a slightly revised operational approach we think will satisfy procurement/legal while keeping incentives aligned.

1) Proration math: we will pro-rate at the token-unit level using billed tokens for the invoice period. Example tab in the attached workbook shows per-day token average x remaining days in billing cycle to compute the partial-month adjustment. We will include an "Invoice detail" CSV on each invoice containing the token breakout for audit.

2) Rebate verification metric: billed tokens (post any consumption-based discounts) is our canonical metric; we can provide a token-export for the quarter for your finance team to reconcile.

3) Rebate release cadence: propose we put rebate accrual on a quarterly basis but release it as a credit after legal acceptance of quarterly reconciliation reports (standard SLA 7 business days to produce). If you prefer immediate credit we can do that but require a short-term escrow hold to handle disputes.

4) Legal review window: 10 business days is fine. We will hold price in the proposed amendment pending legal review as long as the PO is issued within 10 business days of the amendment date. If PO is delayed beyond that we can keep the earlier pricing for one additional 30-day grace window.

5) Payment terms: net45 is acceptable. For early-payment discount, we can offer a 1.5% settlement discount if paid within net10.

Operational request (to procurement): if you pick Option 1 (accelerated uplift + rebate) we need an expected consumption forecast by quarter to size GPU reserved capacity and make the dedicated-infra commitments. If you go Option 2 (staged top-up) we will reserve half the uplift immediately and target the remaining capacity for the co-term date.

I attached a short "ops checklist" and the amended proposal as PDF (MA_plan_draft.pdf) that includes the conditional rebate language and an example invoice.

If that aligns, Kimberly and I can prepare the amendment + DocuSign and get it to your legal team.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Sales Director | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal uplift & commit velocity — conditional rebate scheduler

Thanks Kimberly and Ben — that all helps. Procurement is comfortable moving forward with Option 2 (Staged Top-up & Co-term) on these conditions:

- We will issue the PO by 2027-07-01.
- Legal will need the amendment in DocuSign form; they require the full 10-business-day review once we receive the DocuSign packet.
- HealthlyX accepts the staged billing (50% now, 50% at co-term) and the 5% guaranteed discount; we will request the operational credit language for unused top-up to be explicit in the amendment.

Please send the DocuSign link and the finalized amendment PDF and we’ll route to legal and procurement. If all goes well we’ll be signed and POed by July 1.

—Alex
